arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Palazzolo's counsel cited Armstrong v. United States. They argued the Just Compensation Clause bars unfair burdens. They stated the government cannot force one person to pay for public needs.
Rhode Island's counsel emphasized the timing of the regulations. They noted the rules existed before Palazzolo bought the land. They argued he assumed these risks when he purchased the property.
Palazzolo's counsel addressed the scope of the property interest. They asked if courts should look only at wetlands. They suggested the upland area matters for the compensation claim.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Anthony Palazzolo bought 18 acres in Rhode Island. State rules barred him from filling wetlands. He claims this regulation took his property without just compensation. Rhode Island argues the rules predated his ownership. The Court must decide if the Just Compensation Clause applies to later buyers.
